target.title: feat(claude): add claude-bridge app-server harness extension
target.body:
## Summary

TL;DR:
Inspiration: https://openclaw.ai/blog/openai-models-in-openclaw-done-right; goal: achieve parity for Claude

New feature; issue https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/93793

OpenClaw currently has no first-class harness for Anthropic models. Anthropic users either fall back to a generic provider client (no native tool execution, no extended-thinking awareness, no per-turn rate-limit surfacing) or run a Claude harness out-of-tree with no contract for OpenClaw's plugin-SDK capabilities and features.

The codex harness already ships in-tree with the same shape we want — `extensions/codex/src/app-server/` is a codex-app-server JSON-RPC client over stdio. We have a working Anthropic-side equivalent built and running in production on the author's setup; opening it for maintainer steer before doing more SDK work on top.

Harness: this PR
JSON-RPC server: https://www.npmjs.com/package/@zeroaltitude/openclaw-claude-bridge

**What is the intended outcome?**

- Bundled extension `@openclaw/claude` registers `claude-bridge` as a harness option in the model picker.
- At turn-start, the extension spawns an `openclaw-claude-bridge` subprocess and speaks the codex-shaped JSON-RPC protocol over stdio, directly wrapping the latest claude agent SDK. The server (currently published as `@zeroaltitude/openclaw-claude-bridge`  https://www.npmjs.com/package/@zeroaltitude/openclaw-claude-bridge — fork-preview path; would migrate to `@openclaw/openclaw-claude-bridge` if the maintainers republish it) handles Anthropic API I/O, rate-limit surfacing, image-payload sanitization, and plugin-thread-config persistence.
- Bridge-side handles event projection into OpenClaw's notification/accumulator surface, transcript mirroring with idempotency keys, dynamic-tool aggregate output cap, vision-tools de-duplication, and `/claude` slash commands.
- See `extensions/claude/README.md` for the full feature map.

**What is intentionally out of scope?**

- Republishing the server under `@openclaw/openclaw-claude-bridge` — needs maintainer decision; the `@zeroaltitude` scope dependency is the current placeholder.
- Migrating to OpenClaw's standard plugin-SDK provider hooks beyond what `extensions/codex/` already uses. The bridge follows codex's pattern verbatim where applicable.
- Anything outside the harness bridge surface.

**What does success look like?** Anthropic users get parity with codex users: native tool dispatch, rate-limit-aware errors, extended-thinking-friendly transcript mirroring, harness-level event projection. No regressions to existing harnesses.

**What should reviewers focus on?**

1. **Scope concern — am I taking too much core?** The branch touches `src/plugins/command-registration.ts`, `src/plugins/current-plugin-metadata-snapshot.ts`, `src/plugins/agent-tool-result-middleware-types.ts`, `src/auto-reply/reply/get-reply-native-slash-fast-path.ts`, `src/agents/model-runtime-aliases.ts`, and `src/agents/tools/image-tool.ts`. Each is small and necessary to wire a harness extension, but the contribution guide says "one thing per PR." Happy to split into prep PRs first if maintainers prefer.
2. **External-plugin vs. bundled-extension** — Per CONTRIBUTING.md "most features should be third-party plugins." Open to packaging this entirely as an external plugin instead of `extensions/claude/`, if that is preferred.
3. **Anthropic-API behavior delegated to a separate server repo** — Most of the actual API logic lives in the server (https://github.com/zeroaltitude/openclaw-plugins/tree/main/openclaw-claude/server -- https://www.npmjs.com/package/@zeroaltitude/openclaw-claude-bridge). Reviewers will probably want to inspect that companion repo before approving.
4. **`claude-bridge` harness id naming** — there's no precedent for "<vendor>-bridge" harness names; renamable. (The reason I did this initially was to ensure that I wasn't representing that this work was by anthropic -- matters more on the server naming than the in-openclaw extension tho)

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Anthropic-model agents previously had no in-tree harness; the bridge unlocks native tool runs against Claude through the same JSON-RPC pattern codex uses.
- **Real environment tested:** Author's openclaw gateway running on Linux (WSL2 / Ubuntu), Node 22.x. Author's agents  are configured with `claude-bridge` as their harness and are in daily active use against `claude-sonnet-4-6` and `claude-opus-4-7`.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**
  1. `pnpm install && pnpm build`
  2. `openclaw gateway restart --deep`
  3. Send a Slack DM to one of the claude-bridge agents
  4. Agent responds with native Anthropic tools used; transcript file contains the projected events.
  5. `/claude status` in the same thread prints shared-client liveness.
- **Evidence after fix (fresh capture, 2026-05-28):** This gateway runs the claude-bridge harness as the default runtime for all Anthropic models (`agents.defaults.models.*.agentRuntime.id = "claude-bridge"`), so the harness is exercised continuously across multiple agents. Captured live:
  1. **Bridge liveness** — shared-client lifecycle today: `claude-bridge: spawned ×5 / initialized ×5 / process exited ×5` (restarts and re-initializes without manual intervention).
  2. **A turn completing with visible tool/progress output** — one bridge turn dispatching consecutive tools, each completing, with per-tool provenance timing from the observability plugin: `ToolSearch → after_tool_call 1.9ms`, `exec → 1.7ms`, `Write → 1.9ms`, `Agent → 1.9ms`.
  3. **Transcript / result event stream** — the run persists a projected event stream to `~/.openclaw/agents/<id>/sessions/<uuid>.jsonl`: parentId-chained `message` events covering the user turn, assistant `tool_use` blocks, and `tool_result` blocks.
  4. **`/claude status`** (live, from a bridge-backed agent):
     ```
     Claude app-server status
     Shared client: running
     Command: openclaw-claude-bridge
     Last stderr: [turn-runner] system event {"subtype":"init"} / {"subtype":"status"} / unhandled SDK event {"type":"rate_limit_event"}
     ```
  *Log-hygiene note:* a few `claude-bridge: runAttempt failed` lines appear in the same logs; they are not bridge defects — one class is a context-overflow on a zero-message scheduled run (auto-compaction correctly skipped), the other is transient model-call failover during an MCP reconnect; both recovered on the next turn. Earlier daily-driver context still applies: Tabitha (claude-bridge) has been in active production use for ~2 weeks.
- **Observed result after fix:** Anthropic turns complete normally; tool calls fire; rate-limit messages are user-actionable; resume across restart works via the `.claude-binding.json` sidecar.
- **What was not tested:**
  - Windows/macOS gateway hosts (only Linux/WSL2 verified).
  - Bun runtime (Node 22 only).
  - Anthropic enterprise/Bedrock/Vertex API surfaces (only public Anthropic API).
  - Concurrent multi-account scenarios beyond 3 agents.
- **Proof limitations or environment constraints:** Author runs a single-host gateway. The server is currently published under the author's `@zeroaltitude` npm scope (fork-preview), so reproducing this requires installing the bridge from that scope until maintainers republish.
- **Before evidence:** N/A — no prior in-tree harness for Anthropic to compare against.

## Tests and validation

- Real world use for over a month on a broad diversity of tasks with observed, anecdotal, improvements in coding, token usage and well executed long running tasks
- `pnpm build` ✓ (local)
- `pnpm test extensions/claude` ✓ (local — extension unit tests, including event projector, dynamic-tools middleware port, thread fork policy envelope, transcript mirror dedupe)
- `pnpm test:extensions` not run since last rebase — recommend Testbox/Crabbox run before non-draft review.
- No `CHANGELOG.md` edit per contributor rule; maintainer to add on land.

## Risk checklist

- **Did user-visible behavior change?** Yes — new `claude-bridge` harness appears in model picker; new `/claude` slash command surface.
- **Did config, environment, or migration behavior change?** Yes — new plugin `configSchema` (see `extensions/claude/openclaw.plugin.json`). Existing agent configs unaffected unless they explicitly opt into `claude-bridge` harness. Doctor contract added (`extensions/claude/doctor-contract-api.ts`).
- **Did security, auth, secrets, network, or tool execution behavior change?** Yes (intentional). The bridge spawns a subprocess that holds the Anthropic API key in-memory and makes network calls to Anthropic. Subprocess lifecycle is owned by the harness, not user shell. The plugin SDK enabler changes (e.g. `command-registration.ts`) are additive and follow existing codex-extension precedent.
- **Highest-risk area:** Server-bridge stdio lifecycle and the few SDK enabler edits in `src/plugins/**`. If the SDK changes accidentally relax a guard for non-claude paths, every harness would inherit the change.
- **How is that risk mitigated?** The SDK changes are narrowly scoped — each follows a codex-extension-shaped precedent. Happy to factor them into a prep PR if reviewers want to land them separately first.

## Current review state

- **Next action:** Maintainer steer on scope: (a) accept as bundled extension as-is, (b) split SDK enablers into a prep PR first, or (c) request packaging as an external plugin.
- **Still waiting on:** Maintainer decision on the above. CI run on this push.
- **Bot/reviewer comments addressed:** None yet — opening draft.

---

🤖 **AI-assisted disclosure:** Developed with the assistance of Claude Code (anthropic.com/claude-code). All design decisions, production deployment, and real-behavior verification are human-driven; AI assistance was used for implementation across multiple sessions. Session transcripts available on request.

target.title: feat(signal): show status reactions during inbound replies
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Signal users could receive a normal agent reply without the lifecycle status reactions already available in other message channels. When status reactions are configured, Signal can now show that an inbound message was acknowledged, is being processed, is using tools or compacting, has stalled, and then completed or failed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Signal inbound handling now uses the shared status-reaction controller behind the existing `messages.statusReactions.enabled`, acknowledgement scope, and Signal `reactionLevel` gates. Direct messages react to the inbound sender/timestamp; group messages react through the group id plus the original message author; reaction send/remove failures are logged without blocking the agent dispatch path.

The shared dispatch path also forwards opted-in compaction lifecycle callbacks when normal progress text is hidden, so reaction-only progress can still move through compacting and back to thinking.

The observed `⏳` hourglass is intentional. It is the shared soft-stall status (`stallSoft`) from the default status-reaction timing, so it can appear during longer turns before the final success/error state.

## User Impact

Configured Signal routes can show live status reactions during an agent turn instead of only typing/read feedback. Replies that are sent through message tools are treated as successful visible replies, so the final status does not incorrectly flash as an error when the reply was delivered through that path.

## Evidence

Manual Signal proof:

- Used only the scratch manual-test config and the intended Testing realm / paired Signal setup; real `~/.openclaw` was not touched.
- Corrected the scratch provider to `atlassian-ai-gateway/gpt-5.5-2026-04-23` on `http://127.0.0.1:19090/v1` before the successful proof.
- Jesse sent `hey` in Testing realm. The visible lifecycle showed acknowledgement/thinking status, typing, the expected hourglass soft-stall status, final status, and a delivered reply.

target.title: feat(sessions): add read-only diagnose command
target.body:
Closes #94175
Supersedes #94192 (closed after the fork branch disappeared, not because the change was rejected).
Related: #86159, #88870, #77542

## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw operators currently have to piece together `sessions`, `sessions tail`, health output, logs, and Gateway state when a session looks stuck, silent, queued, terminal, or missing transcript evidence. That makes incident triage slow and risky, especially before using recovery actions that could disturb active work.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds an additive, read-only `sessions.diagnose` Gateway RPC with `operator.read` scope and a matching `openclaw sessions diagnose` CLI command. The diagnosis combines stored session state, visible Gateway runs, embedded-run state, diagnostic activity, command-lane state, bounded transcript metadata, and generic delivery metadata into stable finding codes.

The scope is intentionally conservative: no recovery, aborts, lane release, config/env changes, provider/channel connectivity checks, or changelog edit. The command rejects ambiguous selectors and avoids raw transcript content, secrets, and local transcript paths.

## User Impact

Users and operators can run one command to understand whether a session is active, queued, stale, terminal, missing transcript evidence, unresolved, or simply not found before taking any recovery action. Bug reports can also include structured diagnosis output instead of scattered logs.

## Evidence

target.title: fix(net-policy): preserve diagnostics after redacted URL query secrets
target.body:
﻿## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where redacting sensitive query values from URL-like diagnostic text could remove the trailing error detail after the secret value.

The fallback path in `redactSensitiveUrlLikeString()` handles arbitrary text that is not parseable as one complete URL. Its query-value regex previously consumed until `&`, so text such as:

```text
failed https://x.test/cb?token=abc timed out
```

could be reduced to:

```text
failed https://x.test/cb?token=***
```

That masked the secret, but it also dropped the useful diagnostic suffix: `timed out`.

## Why This Change Was Made

This change keeps the redaction behavior narrow: sensitive query values are still replaced with `***`, but fallback matching stops before surrounding prose, whitespace, or common delimiters.

After reviewer feedback, the fallback also consumes quoted query values before preserving the surrounding prose, so `?token="abc"` becomes `?token="***"` instead of leaving the quoted value visible.

The parseable full-URL path remains unchanged. This only tightens the heuristic fallback used for URL-like substrings inside larger diagnostic messages.

## User Impact

Operators and developers keep the remediation context in logs and CLI errors while secrets are still hidden.

For example, a message like:

```text
failed https://x.test/cb?token=abc timed out
```

now becomes:

```text
failed https://x.test/cb?token=*** timed out
```

instead of losing the timeout reason.

## Evidence

Added focused regression tests in `packages/net-policy/src/redact-sensitive-url.test.ts` for arbitrary diagnostic text with sensitive query parameters followed by prose, quoted values, and bracket/delimiter-wrapped diagnostics.

Validation run:

```powershell
$env:CI='true'
pnpm exec vitest run --config test/vitest/vitest.unit.config.ts packages/net-policy/src/redact-sensitive-url.test.ts
```

Result:

```text
Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests       19 passed (19)
```

Real diagnostic path proof through `resolveHttpMcpServerLaunchConfig()` in `src/agents/mcp-http.ts`, run against the PR branch with malformed HTTP MCP URLs so the production invalid-URL diagnostic path calls `redactSensitiveUrlLikeString()`:

```powershell
node --import tsx .artifacts\net-policy-real-call-path-proof.mjs
```

Output:

```text
its url is not a valid URL: https://[bad-host/cb?token=*** timed out
its url is not a valid URL: https://[bad-host/cb?token="***" timed out
its url is not a valid URL: https://[bad-host/cb?token=***), retrying
```

Relevant call chain:

```text
HTTP MCP config validation
  -> resolveHttpMcpServerLaunchConfig(...)
  -> invalid URL diagnostic reason
  -> redactSensitiveUrlLikeString(...)
  -> fallback URL-like query redaction
  -> sensitive query value replacement
```

Non-goals:

- This does not replace the fallback with a full URL lexer.
- This does not change userinfo redaction.
- This does not broaden which query names are considered sensitive.

AI-assisted: Yes, prepared with Codex GPT-5.5 xhigh review assistance.

target.title: Add Telegram late-dispatch proof scenario
target.body:
Related: #87299
Related: #89930

## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a Telegram late-dispatch boundary where a visible final reply could be followed by a generic error fallback if dispatch cleanup failed afterward.

The branch had also become unmergeable after upstream Telegram dispatch changes. This update rebases the proof harness onto current `origin/main`, resolves the conflicts, and keeps the fallback suppression tied to final-answer delivery rather than any partial/progress delivery.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds a trusted private-QA proof scenario, `--proof-scenario late-dispatch-after-final`, and passes it into the local Telegram gateway as `OPENCLAW_TELEGRAM_QA_DISPATCH_FAULT=late-dispatch-after-final`. The Telegram hook remains gated by `OPENCLAW_BUILD_PRIVATE_QA=1`, `OPENCLAW_ENABLE_PRIVATE_QA_CLI=1`, and the exact scenario value.

The proof runner also rejects candidate SUT checkouts that do not contain the matching Telegram QA fault hook, and the Mantis Telegram Desktop prompt tells agents to rebase onto the harness or test a merge result instead of treating an unsupported candidate run as proof. The SUT support guard now checks for the hook in the exported `dispatchTelegramMessage` dispatch path rather than accepting loose stale strings or fake dispatcher snippets (RF-003). The runtime fallback guard now suppresses duplicate generic fallback only after a final answer has been delivered, while preserving the error fallback after partial-only output failures. Spooled replay completion still treats already visible output as delivered so draft/progress output is not retried unnecessarily.

Maintainers should still decide whether carrying this private-QA runtime hook and trusted proof-runner behavior in bundled Telegram source is acceptable (RF-004, RF-005).

## User Impact

Developers and maintainers can now run a deterministic Telegram proof scenario for the late-dispatch-after-final boundary, and proof agents get a clear failure instead of misleading exact-path evidence when a candidate checkout lacks the hook.

Telegram users no longer receive a second generic error reply after a visible final answer is already delivered. If dispatch fails after only partial/block output, the existing terminal error fallback is still sent.

## Evidence

Before this update, `check-main-drift` reported `has_conflicts: true` and `sync-main` reproduced conflicts in:

- `extensions/telegram/src/bot-message-dispatch.ts`
- `extensions/telegram/src/bot-message-dispatch.test.ts`
- `scripts/e2e/telegram-user-crabbox-proof.ts`
- `test/scripts/telegram-user-crabbox-proof.test.ts`

After resolving the conflicts, `check-main-drift` reports `has_conflicts: false` against current `origin/main`; the updated branch is squashed to a single commit on top of `origin/main` (RF-002). Validation included the rebased full-file suites before the final focused guard hardening:

```text
$ pnpm exec vitest run extensions/telegram/src/bot-message-dispatch.test.ts
Test Files  1 passed (1)
     Tests  147 passed (147)
  Duration  18.83s

$ pnpm exec vitest run test/scripts/telegram-user-crabbox-proof.test.ts
Test Files  1 passed (1)
     Tests  32 passed (32)
  Duration  4.98s

$ pnpm run check:no-conflict-markers
$ node scripts/check-no-conflict-markers.mjs
```

Additional focused validation on the current head:

```text
$ pnpm exec vitest run test/scripts/telegram-user-crabbox-proof.test.ts -t "fake dispatcher option block|cleans local SUT children"
Test Files  1 passed (1)
     Tests  2 passed | 31 skipped (33)
  Duration  2.10s

$ pnpm exec vitest run extensions/telegram/src/bot-message-dispatch.test.ts -t "does not return retryable after spooled replay already showed visible output|returns retryable when dispatch fails after partial output and the fallback is not delivered|returns retryable when spooled replay suppresses fallback after non-silent delivery skip"
Test Files  1 passed (1)
     Tests  3 passed | 145 skipped (148)
  Duration  17.68s

$ git diff --check
```

Current limitations: this PR still does not include a fresh live Telegram Desktop forced late-dispatch capture (RF-001). The intended exact-path consumer remains the downstream Telegram behavior-fix proof after this harness lands or is tested as a merge result.

target.title: fix: require Android contact and calendar write permissions in onboarding
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Android onboarding could show Contacts or Calendar as authorized after only the read permission was granted, even though the app requests both read and write permissions from that row.

That left onboarding out of sync with the rest of the Android app: Settings already treats Contacts and Calendar as granted only when both read and write permissions are present, and the actual Contacts/Calendar add handlers require the write permission before they can create records.

This also fixes the filtered callback case. The onboarding request helper filters out permissions that are already granted before launching `RequestMultiplePermissions`; if READ was granted first and WRITE was granted later, the callback map can contain only WRITE. The state merge now uses the callback result plus the current system grant state for the omitted permission.

AI-assisted: yes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The previous onboarding state used only `READ_CONTACTS` and `READ_CALENDAR` for initial grant status, and the ActivityResult callback also only looked at those read permissions.

This change adds a focused read/write permission merge helper and uses it for Contacts and Calendar onboarding state. Initial state now requires both read and write permissions, and callback state now preserves already-granted permissions that were filtered out before the request was launched.

## User Impact

Users will no longer see Contacts or Calendar marked as ready in Android onboarding until the permissions needed by both read and add workflows are actually available. Users who grant the two permissions in separate prompts should now see the row update correctly once the missing permission is granted.

## Evidence

- `cd apps/android && ./gradlew :app:testThirdPartyDebugUnitTest --tests ai.openclaw.app.ui.OnboardingFlowLogicTest`
- `cd apps/android && ./gradlew :app:testPlayDebugUnitTest --tests ai.openclaw.app.ui.OnboardingFlowLogicTest`
- `git diff --check`
- `.agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode local`

target.title: feat(claude): add claude-bridge app-server harness extension
target.body:
## Summary

TL;DR:
Inspiration: https://openclaw.ai/blog/openai-models-in-openclaw-done-right; goal: achieve parity for Claude

New feature; issue https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/93793

OpenClaw currently has no first-class harness for Anthropic models. Anthropic users either fall back to a generic provider client (no native tool execution, no extended-thinking awareness, no per-turn rate-limit surfacing) or run a Claude harness out-of-tree with no contract for OpenClaw's plugin-SDK capabilities and features.

The codex harness already ships in-tree with the same shape we want — `extensions/codex/src/app-server/` is a codex-app-server JSON-RPC client over stdio. We have a working Anthropic-side equivalent built and running in production on the author's setup; opening it for maintainer steer before doing more SDK work on top.

Harness: this PR
JSON-RPC server: https://www.npmjs.com/package/@zeroaltitude/openclaw-claude-bridge

**What is the intended outcome?**

- Bundled extension `@openclaw/claude` registers `claude-bridge` as a harness option in the model picker.
- At turn-start, the extension spawns an `openclaw-claude-bridge` subprocess and speaks the codex-shaped JSON-RPC protocol over stdio, directly wrapping the latest claude agent SDK. The server (currently published as `@zeroaltitude/openclaw-claude-bridge`  https://www.npmjs.com/package/@zeroaltitude/openclaw-claude-bridge — fork-preview path; would migrate to `@openclaw/openclaw-claude-bridge` if the maintainers republish it) handles Anthropic API I/O, rate-limit surfacing, image-payload sanitization, and plugin-thread-config persistence.
- Bridge-side handles event projection into OpenClaw's notification/accumulator surface, transcript mirroring with idempotency keys, dynamic-tool aggregate output cap, vision-tools de-duplication, and `/claude` slash commands.
- See `extensions/claude/README.md` for the full feature map.

**What is intentionally out of scope?**

- Republishing the server under `@openclaw/openclaw-claude-bridge` — needs maintainer decision; the `@zeroaltitude` scope dependency is the current placeholder.
- Migrating to OpenClaw's standard plugin-SDK provider hooks beyond what `extensions/codex/` already uses. The bridge follows codex's pattern verbatim where applicable.
- Anything outside the harness bridge surface.

**What does success look like?** Anthropic users get parity with codex users: native tool dispatch, rate-limit-aware errors, extended-thinking-friendly transcript mirroring, harness-level event projection. No regressions to existing harnesses.

**What should reviewers focus on?**

1. **Scope concern — am I taking too much core?** The branch touches `src/plugins/command-registration.ts`, `src/plugins/current-plugin-metadata-snapshot.ts`, `src/plugins/agent-tool-result-middleware-types.ts`, `src/auto-reply/reply/get-reply-native-slash-fast-path.ts`, `src/agents/model-runtime-aliases.ts`, and `src/agents/tools/image-tool.ts`. Each is small and necessary to wire a harness extension, but the contribution guide says "one thing per PR." Happy to split into prep PRs first if maintainers prefer.
2. **External-plugin vs. bundled-extension** — Per CONTRIBUTING.md "most features should be third-party plugins." Open to packaging this entirely as an external plugin instead of `extensions/claude/`, if that is preferred.
3. **Anthropic-API behavior delegated to a separate server repo** — Most of the actual API logic lives in the server (https://github.com/zeroaltitude/openclaw-plugins/tree/main/openclaw-claude/server -- https://www.npmjs.com/package/@zeroaltitude/openclaw-claude-bridge). Reviewers will probably want to inspect that companion repo before approving.
4. **`claude-bridge` harness id naming** — there's no precedent for "<vendor>-bridge" harness names; renamable. (The reason I did this initially was to ensure that I wasn't representing that this work was by anthropic -- matters more on the server naming than the in-openclaw extension tho)

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Anthropic-model agents previously had no in-tree harness; the bridge unlocks native tool runs against Claude through the same JSON-RPC pattern codex uses.
- **Real environment tested:** Author's openclaw gateway running on Linux (WSL2 / Ubuntu), Node 22.x. Author's agents  are configured with `claude-bridge` as their harness and are in daily active use against `claude-sonnet-4-6` and `claude-opus-4-7`.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**
  1. `pnpm install && pnpm build`
  2. `openclaw gateway restart --deep`
  3. Send a Slack DM to one of the claude-bridge agents
  4. Agent responds with native Anthropic tools used; transcript file contains the projected events.
  5. `/claude status` in the same thread prints shared-client liveness.
- **Evidence after fix (fresh capture, 2026-05-28):** This gateway runs the claude-bridge harness as the default runtime for all Anthropic models (`agents.defaults.models.*.agentRuntime.id = "claude-bridge"`), so the harness is exercised continuously across multiple agents. Captured live:
  1. **Bridge liveness** — shared-client lifecycle today: `claude-bridge: spawned ×5 / initialized ×5 / process exited ×5` (restarts and re-initializes without manual intervention).
  2. **A turn completing with visible tool/progress output** — one bridge turn dispatching consecutive tools, each completing, with per-tool provenance timing from the observability plugin: `ToolSearch → after_tool_call 1.9ms`, `exec → 1.7ms`, `Write → 1.9ms`, `Agent → 1.9ms`.
  3. **Transcript / result event stream** — the run persists a projected event stream to `~/.openclaw/agents/<id>/sessions/<uuid>.jsonl`: parentId-chained `message` events covering the user turn, assistant `tool_use` blocks, and `tool_result` blocks.
  4. **`/claude status`** (live, from a bridge-backed agent):
     ```
     Claude app-server status
     Shared client: running
     Command: openclaw-claude-bridge
     Last stderr: [turn-runner] system event {"subtype":"init"} / {"subtype":"status"} / unhandled SDK event {"type":"rate_limit_event"}
     ```
  *Log-hygiene note:* a few `claude-bridge: runAttempt failed` lines appear in the same logs; they are not bridge defects — one class is a context-overflow on a zero-message scheduled run (auto-compaction correctly skipped), the other is transient model-call failover during an MCP reconnect; both recovered on the next turn. Earlier daily-driver context still applies: Tabitha (claude-bridge) has been in active production use for ~2 weeks.
- **Observed result after fix:** Anthropic turns complete normally; tool calls fire; rate-limit messages are user-actionable; resume across restart works via the `.claude-binding.json` sidecar.
- **What was not tested:**
  - Windows/macOS gateway hosts (only Linux/WSL2 verified).
  - Bun runtime (Node 22 only).
  - Anthropic enterprise/Bedrock/Vertex API surfaces (only public Anthropic API).
  - Concurrent multi-account scenarios beyond 3 agents.
- **Proof limitations or environment constraints:** Author runs a single-host gateway. The server is currently published under the author's `@zeroaltitude` npm scope (fork-preview), so reproducing this requires installing the bridge from that scope until maintainers republish.
- **Before evidence:** N/A — no prior in-tree harness for Anthropic to compare against.

## Tests and validation

- Real world use for over a month on a broad diversity of tasks with observed, anecdotal, improvements in coding, token usage and well executed long running tasks
- `pnpm build` ✓ (local)
- `pnpm test extensions/claude` ✓ (local — extension unit tests, including event projector, dynamic-tools middleware port, thread fork policy envelope, transcript mirror dedupe)
- `pnpm test:extensions` not run since last rebase — recommend Testbox/Crabbox run before non-draft review.
- No `CHANGELOG.md` edit per contributor rule; maintainer to add on land.

## Risk checklist

- **Did user-visible behavior change?** Yes — new `claude-bridge` harness appears in model picker; new `/claude` slash command surface.
- **Did config, environment, or migration behavior change?** Yes — new plugin `configSchema` (see `extensions/claude/openclaw.plugin.json`). Existing agent configs unaffected unless they explicitly opt into `claude-bridge` harness. Doctor contract added (`extensions/claude/doctor-contract-api.ts`).
- **Did security, auth, secrets, network, or tool execution behavior change?** Yes (intentional). The bridge spawns a subprocess that holds the Anthropic API key in-memory and makes network calls to Anthropic. Subprocess lifecycle is owned by the harness, not user shell. The plugin SDK enabler changes (e.g. `command-registration.ts`) are additive and follow existing codex-extension precedent.
- **Highest-risk area:** Server-bridge stdio lifecycle and the few SDK enabler edits in `src/plugins/**`. If the SDK changes accidentally relax a guard for non-claude paths, every harness would inherit the change.
- **How is that risk mitigated?** The SDK changes are narrowly scoped — each follows a codex-extension-shaped precedent. Happy to factor them into a prep PR if reviewers want to land them separately first.

## Current review state

- **Next action:** Maintainer steer on scope: (a) accept as bundled extension as-is, (b) split SDK enablers into a prep PR first, or (c) request packaging as an external plugin.
- **Still waiting on:** Maintainer decision on the above. CI run on this push.
- **Bot/reviewer comments addressed:** None yet — opening draft.

---

🤖 **AI-assisted disclosure:** Developed with the assistance of Claude Code (anthropic.com/claude-code). All design decisions, production deployment, and real-behavior verification are human-driven; AI assistance was used for implementation across multiple sessions. Session transcripts available on request.
